info.title: Ownkube CLI API
info.description: API for the Ownkube CLI tool. Authenticate via browser-based flow, then use x-api-key header for subsequent requests.

organizations.description: Organizations this user belongs to. Pass an `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when membership is plural.

quickCreateUrl.description: Open in a browser and click Create stack (handoff mode)

AwsConnectTemplate.description: Deploy this stack yourself with AWS creds already in your environment (autonomous mode). Parameter keys match the template exactly.

awsAccountId.description: 12-digit AWS account ID once the stack reports in

status.description: pending (waiting on the stack) / configuring (provisioning access) / verified / failed

code.description: Raw CloudFormation status code this maps from

kind.description: How to recover: `retry` (transient/propagation, re-verify or re-launch the same stack), `quota` (fix an AWS limit then re-verify), `conflict` (account claimed elsewhere, use a different account).

description.description: What happened and what to do next

AwsConnectionFailure.description: Structured failure + remediation when status is `failed`

slug.description: Lowercase, starts with a letter; letters, numbers, hyphens only.

secret.description: Mark as secret so the value is never returned on reads. Echo a saved secret back with an empty `value` to keep the previous value.

env.description: The full shared env-var set for the environment (replaces the existing set). Every cluster-bound app in the environment is redeployed to apply it.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: API key issued by the browser-based CLI authorization flow.

get.description: Returns the profile of the user associated with the provided API key.

get.summary: List organizations the API key's user belongs to
get.description: Use the returned `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when your account belongs to more than one org.

post.description: Mints a cross-account access request and returns the CloudFormation artifacts. Reuses this org's in-flight (unproven) row, so repeated calls do not pile up records. Poll GET /v1/aws/accounts/{accountId} until status is `verified` or `failed`.

delete.description: Blocked while any cluster still references the account (the cross-account role is required to tear infra down). Destroy those clusters first.

post.description: Normally the stack's phone-home finalizes the connection automatically. Call this to force a verify, optionally passing `awsAccountId` to assume the role directly before the callback arrives.

schema.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.

parameters.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.
parameters.name: awsAccountId

post.summary: Re-arm an account whose access stack was removed
post.description: Re-arms the existing row in place (same external ID and account ID) and returns a fresh CloudFormation link. Re-running the stack recreates the role and re-verifies the same account — no duplicate is created.

post.summary: Re-run account setup on a verified account
post.description: Re-applies the shared roles and policies for an already-verified account. Safe to call to pick up an available upgrade (`needsUpgrade: true`).

get.summary: List clusters in the current organization

post.description: Provisions a cluster (`clusterType` `eks` = Production, `k3s` = Starter) into a verified AWS account (`cloudAccountId`). Returns immediately with a `clusterId` and `status: creating`; poll `/v1/clusters/{clusterId}/status` until it reports `active` or `failed`.

delete.description: Tears the cluster down. Blocked when the cluster still has active deployments unless `force=true` is passed.

schema.description: Destroy even when the cluster still has active deployments. Defaults to false.

parameters.description: Destroy even when the cluster still has active deployments. Defaults to false.
parameters.name: force

get.summary: Get a cluster's live provisioning status
get.description: Lightweight poll target during create/destroy: status, message, and provisioning progress without the full row.

post.description: Valid only while the cluster is still `creating`.

get.summary: List environments in the current organization
get.description: Default `Development` and `Production` environments are auto-seeded for orgs that have none yet, so this endpoint always returns at least two rows.

patch.summary: Update an environment's name, color, or description

delete.description: Soft-deletes the environment. Blocked with `412` if any deployments still reference it.

put.summary: Replace an environment's shared env vars
put.description: Replaces the environment's shared env-var set and redeploys every cluster-bound app that inherits them so the change takes effect immediately.

get.summary: List deployments by environment or cluster
get.description: Pass `environmentId` to scope to one environment, or `clusterId` to scope to one cluster. Exactly one is required.

post.description: Creates a deployment. The body is a discriminated union on `resourceType` (`web`, `worker`, `job`, `database`, `function`); each type carries its own `config` block. Omit `clusterId` on a cluster-bound type to deploy onto the org's shared cluster.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the deployment and tears down its cluster resources. Functions hand off to an async teardown and report `deleting` until it finalizes.

patch.description: Updates a cluster-bound deployment (web/worker/job/database) and records a revision. Send the config block matching the deployment's type: `appConfig` for web/worker, `jobConfig` for job, `databaseConfig` for database. Use the function update endpoint for functions.

get.description: Reads log lines from the in-cluster logs backend over the requested window. `filter` accepts a LogsQL regex matched against the message body.
Returns the host, port, credentials, and connection URI for a database deployment. Only valid for `resourceType: database`.

patch.description: Updates a `function`-type deployment's config (handler, runtime, env, triggers) and records a revision.

post.description: Upgrades a cluster-bound deployment to a newer platform version and resyncs. Downgrades are rejected. Use the function platform-version endpoint for functions.
Upgrades a `function`-type deployment to a newer platform version and resyncs.

post.summary: Copy a deployment to another environment
post.description: Clones this deployment's current config into `targetEnvironmentId` on `targetClusterId`, creating a new deployment. Not valid for functions.
Rotates the owner-role password of a `database`-type deployment and returns the new password. The response intentionally contains the live credential.

get.summary: List a scheduled job's recent runs
get.description: Reads the CronJob and its spawned runs live from the cluster. Non-job deployments return an empty, non-existent history rather than erroring.

post.description: Spawns a one-off run of a `job`-type deployment off-schedule and returns the created Job name.

delete.description: Deletes the named run's Job (terminating its Pods). The named Job must belong to this deployment's CronJob.

get.description: Lists the platform versions published for a `clusterType` + `resourceType` pair, newest first. Use these values with the platform-version upgrade endpoint.
Lists the platform versions published for functions, newest first.

get.summary: List revisions for a deployment (newest first)

post.summary: Roll a deployment back to a prior revision
post.description: Restores the config snapshot from `revisionId` onto the deployment and records a new revision. Returns the new revision.

post.summary: Promote a deployment's config to another deployment
post.description: Copies this deployment's current config into `targetDeploymentId`, records a revision there, and links it back to this deployment's latest revision. Returns the new revision on the target.
